answers.answer: Separate Conflict cards by backs. Shuffle all four Conflict III and place them face down; shuffle the nine Conflict II and deal five face down on top; shuffle the three Conflict I and deal one face down on top. The deck has ten cards, with I on top, five II below, and four III on the bottom. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In four-player play, the human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. In either case the human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in the garrison and nine in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score marker is on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents start on Leader; 3 troops in garrison, remaining 9 in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards remaining in hand that you reveal, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up move all cards in front of you, from both Agent and Reveal turns, to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player Turns and Reveal Turn: may Reveal with Agents left; after Reveal turns are skipped; resolve just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: No: entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving the space or played card effects, so an Agent-box resource gain cannot pay that same entry cost. One card lets you choose only one Agent icon and send one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Agent Turn: costs are paid before effects; ‘You choose only one Agent icon’; no-Agent-icon cards may only be revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, for at most five in this example. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops stay in the garrison and no units deploy. Troops are recruited from your supply into your garrison; deployment is from the garrison (except newly recruited troops can be deployed on that Combat turn).
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit from supply into garrison; at Combat spaces deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on the destination (not your own Agent). Gather Intelligence recalls your Spy from a connected post to draw a card. You cannot use the same Spy for both effects. Choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing your Agent, before receiving space or Agent-card effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence timing is after placement and before effects; same Spy cannot pay both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You may join the Combat Intrigue window only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; with none, you cannot participate.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, sword = 1; no units means strength 0. Combat: only players with at least one unit in the Conflict may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent you acting again after an opponent plays; the window closes once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply, not garrison, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; close after consecutive passes; cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in a four-player Conflict, each receives the second reward; the other players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. With the same tie in a three-player Conflict, each tied player receives the second reward, no other rewards are given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Combat ties: exactly two tied first with four players leaves others competing for third; with three or fewer no other rewards; nobody takes card. Combat says 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles rewards once; a second sandworm does not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to gain it a second time: pay 6 spice total for 2 VP when that doubled reward applies.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more sandworms double; control and battle icons cannot; may pay cost a second time (example: 6 spice for 2 VP).

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply, check it against face-up Conflict or Objective cards in your supply. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP; matching is mandatory. During Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icon types in your supply; flip the pair face down for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: on winning/taking a Conflict, check face-up Conflict or Objective cards; ‘must’ flip match for 1 VP; Endgame wild matches any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is kept if Influence later falls below 4 and is earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance token and gains 1 VP, which is retained only while holding it. Tying the current holder at 4 does not take the Alliance; you must rise above them to transfer it, subject to the separate FAQ rule if the holder loses Influence after a tie.
answers.evidence: Scoring, Faction Influence: 2 VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus persists; Alliance VP tied to holding; tying does not steal token, rising above transfers.

answers.answer: You may spend Reveal-turn Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split Persuasion from one source among different cards. After buying a Row card, replace it from the Imperium Deck, and you may immediately buy that replacement if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: before/between/after Reveal effects; pool or split; Row remains five and replacement may be acquired; card enters discard face up.

answers.answer: At Makers, add 1 spice to each Maker space without an Agent; when visiting a Maker space, gain all bonus spice there. Deep Desert, Hagga Basin and Imperial Basin are Maker spaces. A sandworm can never go in a garrison; it is summoned directly to your Conflict. Maker Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them; Hooks are retained, not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, no sandworm can be summoned to Conflicts at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin; removing it allows summoning to any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers adds spice to empty Maker spaces; Sandworms says direct deployment, Hooks not universal prerequisite; Shield Wall lists protected Conflicts and removal effect.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: game end at round end; resolve Endgame Intrigue first; tiebreak sequence listed.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup puts two contracts face up on the marked board spaces and the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Choosing Shaddam is optional. The ten contrasting-back contracts are the separate Rise of Ix set and stay in the box; they are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup: 20 contracts, two face up and 18 face down; add 4 cards to each deck; Shaddam is optional; contrasting-back 10 are Rise of Ix compatibility set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank contract flipped face up. If all contracts have been taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining its listed spice amount that turn in total, including other sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts: icon takes/replaces; if all taken, 2 Solari; Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire completion definitions.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. Upon completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: already visited space requires a future turn; hold it at placement; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the two eligible Objectives remaining are dealt randomly to the humans, and the human whose Objective shows First Player takes it. First Player alternates only between humans. Each round turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Setup: one Rival, Ornithopter for Rival, humans' Objectives/First Player; turn order; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: When Hagal indicates an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore placement; in either case immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects and apply only revealed Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy procedure; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle when empty or on Reshuffle.

answers.answer: For standard three- or four-player setup, omit Objective cards whose 1-3P/4/6P marking does not match player count, shuffle eligible cards and give one random Objective face up to each player. The player whose card shows the First Player marker takes it. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so cannot be chosen without it.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3 and 5: do not use Shaddam unless using CHOAM; filter by player-count marking and distribute face up; marked Objective determines First Player.

answers.answer: The bank's Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if they run out. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: resources and sandworms are not meant to be limited; take gains from bank and return payments; Recruiting says empty troop supply blocks recruitment.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card, resolve any defensive troop bonus for a controlled location, then each player draws five cards. Recall checks Endgame; if not triggered, players return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference: five phases in order; Round Start reveals Conflict then draws five; Recall checks Endgame and otherwise recalls Agents and passes marker.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying the entry cost and meeting requirements before effects, you may resolve board-space and Agent-box effects in any order, and you also advance Influence on a Faction space. But you cannot use Influence from that visit to meet its own entry requirement, because requirements are checked and cost paid before the visit's effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before resolving effects; then gain space/card effects and advance Faction Influence; these effects may be done in any order.

answers.answer: Normally, an optional arrow cost can be paid only once per turn; the stated exception is sandworm reward doubling applied to a Conflict-card reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory, with exceptions for ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play the Intrigue; you cannot play it without paying all costs.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs: only once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ: mandatory effects/costs exceptions and Intrigue conditions/costs.

answers.answer: A Spy goes from supply onto an unoccupied observation post. If all your Spies are already deployed when you need to place one, you may first recall one for no effect. If a placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type that must be connected to the post, you can place only at a post connected to that icon; otherwise you cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies: place on unoccupied post; with none in supply may recall one for no effect; some effects require a specified connected Agent icon.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent; it only bypasses another player's. You cannot recall a Spy without playing a card for an Agent turn. You may not recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you can use different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies and FAQ Spies: own Agent cannot be bypassed; recall still requires playing a card; two different effects may use two Spies, never two Gather Intelligence on one placement.

answers.answer: Whenever any player, including the controller, visits a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, the controller gains 1 Solari; at Imperial Basin its controller gains 1 spice. Winning the corresponding Conflict grants control by placing your marker and replacing any opponent's marker. When such a Conflict is revealed while you control the location, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: visitor-triggered bonuses and control transfer on winning; defensive troop from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps the first reward and card, with no further rewards. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward and nobody takes the card; with three or fewer players there are no other rewards.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Combat ties and tie table: second-place tie gives third reward to each and winner keeps first/card; third gets nothing; first tie with 3 or fewer gives second reward, no others/card.

answers.answer: In a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second receive their rewards; third receives nothing. This is also the reward rank rule when the third participant is the Rival in a two-human-plus-Rival game: ordinary first and second are paid, and third is not, absent a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second receive rewards; third gets nothing except third reward for a tie for second; includes Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat; Endgame Intrigues only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolving, put them face up in an Intrigue discard pile beside the deck. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Intrigue cards: timing, storage and discard; FAQ Draw timing: when Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle discard to form a new deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless the effect specifies Intrigue. Secrets' Steal Intrigue effect takes one card at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: discard from hand and not Intrigue unless specified; Intrigue cards: each opponent with four or more gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play; trashed cards go to the box, while Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it is a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquire VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing: allowed zones, destinations and optionality; FAQ Victory: The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if card later trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once immediately when you acquire the card, not when you later play it. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be carried over; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box: effect at acquisition; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle discard when deck empty; Persuasion cannot be saved and is lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn are in play together until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond works if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play, so two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play when moved to discard during Clean Up (unless trashed earlier).
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: cards remain in play until Clean Up; one or more other Fremen cards, Bond cards activate mutually regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; the recalled Agent can be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops: ‘Retreat any number’ allows zero.

answers.answer: A freely chosen gain-two-Influence effect applies both Influence to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split between two Factions. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum in its specified Faction. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two different Factions; minimum requirements and Alliance icon conditions are stated.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after two opponents were tied with them, the formerly tied opponent receives the token; if several opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which one receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring, Faction Influence / FAQ Alliance loss: formerly tied player takes token; former holder chooses among several; falling to 3 or lower without 4+ returns token.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue played earlier that has a Reveal effect stays face up until that effect is used at Reveal, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: drawn during Reveal immediately revealed/used; after Reveal kept for next round plus five; Plot stays face up until Reveal effect then discarded.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after you tie for first, because no one wins. If you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: winning-trigger Intrigue cannot be played after tying first; if received as a winning reward it can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP, spice, Solari, water and garrisoned troops all tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: all four resource tiebreakers tied means most recent Reveal wins; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. Complete all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement; they cannot be delayed to a later visit after that placement. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the board-space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held the contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; resolve as Agent-turn effect in any order; must hold it when sending Agent.

answers.answer: No. Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one of those instead of a generally available contract when acquiring a contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe deployment restriction takes effect immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: set-aside contracts do not start in possession and may be chosen when acquiring; Signet Ring restriction immediate, lasts turn not round.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of his Leader's Training track and remains at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with the Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd token start/end; Lady Jessica starts on her side; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on flip turn.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2, and Margot/Irulan can reach 2 with the same Faction again in a game by losing Influence and later regaining it. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up does not trigger Spacing Guild's Favor discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: passing 2 while gaining counts; can reach again after losing/regaining; only moving up counts. Spacing Guild's Favor triggers only when discarded from hand.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon; without CHOAM it draws a card and gives 2 Solari, and with CHOAM it lets you take a contract and replace it. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon; it gives 1 Emperor Influence and takes a contract with CHOAM, or gives 2 Solari without CHOAM. Neither effect itself says to advance an additional Faction track beyond Dutiful Service's stated Emperor Influence; Accept Contract grants no automatic Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract (Spice Trade) and Dutiful Service (Emperor) entries; intro says non-Faction/Landsraad spaces give no automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen is accessed with City, costs nothing, is Combat, and gives the visitor one recruited troop and one card; its controller separately gains 1 Solari. Fremkit uses Fremen, costs nothing, is Combat, grants 1 Fremen Influence and draws one card. Research Station uses City, costs 2 water, is Combat, and recruits two troops and draws two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon one sandworm. Both visits gain all accumulated bonus spice, including if choosing worms. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Deep Desert/Hagga Basin; Sandworm Reward Doubling section says Maker-space visit gains all bonus spice; Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Choose either take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop and gain 1 water; or gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The wall-removal option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr entry.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad and not a Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council entry.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may visit only once per game. Take your third Agent onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster entry.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad, requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari; it is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege entry: Landsraad, 3 Solari, 2+ Emperor, effects listed; no Influence gain stated.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be Guild Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping entry.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari, recruit two troops either way, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; receive 2 Solari free or 4 Solari by paying 1 spice, while its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery entries.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Combat, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics is Combat, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card. Sardaukar is not Combat, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops. Thus Heighliner and Desert Tactics allow normal deployment, while Sardaukar does not.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar, including Combat labels.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad, has no cost, draws an Intrigue and provides 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws a card and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild, has no cost and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even when no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders and Litany Against Fear rulings.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate ruling.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with a color, four Influence cubes at the bottoms of tracks, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival can win: its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall just like a human's.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Setup: starting components and markers; Rival can win and 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's counted resource total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together, each as one. Spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, water; keep leftovers. The threshold is its printed value.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster section.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, whenever the Rival has a set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, it spends each such set for 1 VP. It does not combine different resources into a mixed set of seven.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: exact separate resource sets.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by the leftmost priority icon. Like a human it gains VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP, but does not receive the resource/track bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means the corresponding position in the Rival card's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources/Swordmaster and Rival Agent turns: Rival Influence and numbered-icon rules.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card, select only the destination matching the current condition; if it is occupied, reveal a new Hagal card without using the other destination. The condition is Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination selection conditions and occupied-destination rule.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the Hagal card recruits none. At noncombat spaces newly recruited troops go to its garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence that it lacks does not prevent Agent placement; it simply gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: Combat deploy up to two even when none recruited; noncombat troops to garrison; missing conditional bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes section.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival places its Agent and it then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those recruited troops too. A Place Spy card still does not send an Agent; whether a specified post is available or not, immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: Scheme recruits deploy on same-turn Combat; Place Spy reveals another Hagal card either way.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert, the Rival always collects all accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict where summoning is allowed, it summons one/two worms respectively instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or if the Conflict is protected by the Shield Wall, it summons none and takes base spice instead (2/4 respectively).
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: bonus spice always collected; worm choices and base-spice fallback.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to its strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival can gain control, receives defensive troops when its controlled Conflict is revealed, gains battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards with one or more sandworms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: even with CHOAM, a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section: control, defensive troop, icons, doubling, optional VP, contracts.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total your Combat strength, announce it, and set your marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed during that Reveal turn. Strength over 20 is marked by flipping to the +20 side and starting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: set strength at any point while resolving and update as needed; Strength section explains +20 marker.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: Signet Ring ability activates when played on Agent turn, not reveal; Overview says any card type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recalls you may do without a card, for their specified effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon returns Spy to supply; separate no-card Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence rules.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard-a-card instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: ordinary discard from hand, not Intrigue unless specified.

answers.answer: For a doubled Conflict reward that grants one Influence of your choice, the sandworm doubling lets you take the reward twice, with the same or two different Factions. This is distinct from a single effect granting two free-choice Influence, which must put both on one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example permits 2 Influence with same or two different Factions; Influence says one gain-two effect cannot split.

answers.answer: The Rival resolves the Signet Ring effect printed on its Rival card. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; it takes Agent turns using Hagal effects and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow Rival card's printed Signet Ring; Rival Agent-turn rules say never Reveals.

answers.answer: A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a token from the bank onto the Rival's garrison if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no additional token. Shield Wall removal succeeds only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost and is not Combat. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck. In addition, each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets entry.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost and is Combat. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there; its controller separately gains 1 spice. If the visitor is also controller, that player receives both visit effects, for 2 base-plus-controller spice and all bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin entry; controlled-location note says resolve visitor effects and controller's separate bonus even if same player.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds. Resolve the controlled-location defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. Thus Conflict reveal precedes each player's five-card draw.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start: reveal next Conflict and place atop remaining cards, resolve defense, then draw five.

answers.answer: Each human puts one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. The four Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of those tracks; no player starts holding one. The Shield Wall token starts in its marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on track markers; Wall placed below Spice Refinery; one cube on bottom of each track.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn; turns proceed clockwise, one turn at a time. After Revealing, that player's turns are skipped for the rest of the phase; standard 3–4-player Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, starting with First Player and going clockwise, each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; the window closes after all players involved pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat Intrigue rules.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, then Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists three ordered steps and says effects may be gained in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's ten-card starting deck and place it face down to the left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked Intrigue and Imperium cards before shuffling those decks; deal five Imperium cards face up into the Row and keep the rest face down. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The Combat marker starts at 0; the three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in the player's supply, in clear view.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6, Initial card states: step 6 says place remaining components, including Spies, in supply in clear view; Combat marker at 0.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, use Persuasion to acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. Each cost is shown at the card's top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases occur during Reveal, before, between or after Reveal effects.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: eligible acquisitions, cost location and Reveal-turn timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so you may decline even when a legal placement or recall exists. The Shield Wall detonation icon says you may remove the token, so it is optional; once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies says ordinary placement/recall optional; Shield Wall section says may remove and cannot return.

answers.answer: The destination's upper-left Agent icon must match an Agent icon on the card you play; you choose one icon. A connected Spy alone does not let a City-only card access Shipping. If the card actually has its Spy Agent icon and your Spy is at a post connected to Shipping, you may send the Agent there without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn card-icon rule; Special Rules says connected Spy does not grant all cards access and defines Spy Agent icon.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; any resources it grants before placement join available supply and can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card used to send the Agent or from the destination are gained only after placement and cannot pay that entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot Intrigue may be played before placing Agent and pre-placement gains pay entry; post-placement destination/card gains cannot.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, skip humans who have Revealed but continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Player Turns ends and Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule.

answers.answer: When a Conflict card is revealed for a location you already control, you may immediately deploy one troop from your supply directly to that Conflict, without an Agent visit. After all rewards, each player's Combat marker resets to 0 before the Makers phase.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive troop bonus; Combat cleanup resets all Combat markers to 0.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you, and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve the Agent box, ignoring that card's Reveal box. The described rules do not allow reusing a card already in play or in discard as the card played from hand, or simply moving an Agent already on the board; Agent placement comes from the Leader, and Recall is a separate effect for another Agent.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one hand card face up; send Agent from Leader; use Agent box; Recall Agent returns another board Agent.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent, so he cannot delay it by resolving board-space effects first. The general freedom to order space and Agent-box effects cannot postpone this restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications and FAQ Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring for Agent placement.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no sandworms, first, second and third place receive their printed rewards; fourth receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up after rewards and battle-icon check.
answers.evidence: Combat: with four players ordinary first/second/third receive rewards; highest strength wins and takes Conflict card; zero strength gets none.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You cannot choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Drawing cards: ordinary draw is from own deck; shuffle discard if deck empty.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival. Retain the 2P Reshuffle card; it is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: shuffle House Hagal and place near Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: all tokens in common bank; later-acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: The marker must be adjusted when the Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or strength, during the Combat Intrigue window; Reveal-turn strength is not fixed. After all participants pass consecutively, Combat rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track.
answers.evidence: Combat: adjust marker when Intrigue resolves during window; Reveal total not fixed; resolve Combat using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice or water comes from the bank, not another player's supply. Payments of those resources are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: gains from bank; payments returned to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down first, then flip two face up for the board offers; put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. The summary specifies random shuffling, not player-selected offers or a preset order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle 20 contracts face down, flip two face up, place remaining 18 face down in bank.
